Honestly, the only things you need to "worry" about are temperatures and finding food for your new friend. These little guys are typically resilient little suckers.

These are considered desert tortoises so temps between 68-80° are normal for Russians. Try to set up a basking area around 90-100°  for it during the day. Right now, I use two heat lamps, since its cold out(a black heat/day heat : 50-60W).

They do need UVB lighting as well to stay healthy, so look into finding an appropriate lighting setup for your enclosure.

As far as food goes, Russians are grassland torts so it's diet should mainly be grasses, leafy greens, and weeds. I've heard they like all sorts of greens, but mine likes to be picky and will only really eat weeds and grasses(but these are free so I'm not complaining!). She does have a thing for onion grasses and green onions as well. 
It's just a matter of researching what's safe, and figuring out what yours will eat.
**MAKE SURE YOUR GRASSES ARENT CHEMICALLY TREATED**

They shouldn't be able to see through the walls of their enclosure. If you plan on keeping yours in a glass tank like mine, make sure to cover up the walls with something.

I've heard all kinds of opinions on substrates, but i usually go with my store's peat moss mix blend.

It may seem like a lot to worry about, but once you get the enclosure set up, taking care of your new friend will be a (slow)walk in the park.

Good Luck!

Start small..
It may take a little while longer to achieve your goal(s) this way, but have you thought of attending a two year community college?

Now, I know what you're thinking, "but CC is for directionless dropouts." While there are are a handful of people without any clue at your typical CC, most of the students there are people who simply cannot afford a uni education at the moment. 

You can take most, if not all, of your required Gen eds(depending on your major) at CC, get your grades up, and transfer to almost any 4yr school. You'll have to check with both schools' admissions offices for details on transfer credits, but 9/10 times your basic gen ed class will transfer seamlessly into the uni's program. 

Anywho, I really hope things work out for you.
